traffic spike brute force login flood capacity autoscaler limit

events.statement: auth-service p99 latency was ~90ms (max ~97ms) until 06:44Z, then jumped to ~2800-4100ms from the 06:52Z bucket onward and stayed there through 08:59Z.
auth-service error_rate (HTTP 5xx) was ~0.2% until 06:44Z, then rose to ~13-15% from the 06:52Z bucket onward.
auth-service CPU was ~38% until 06:44Z, then jumped to ~97% (max 99.54%) from 06:52Z onward.
auth-service request_rate was ~390-406 req/s until 06:44Z, then quadrupled to ~1234-1525 req/s from 06:52Z onward.

auth-service logs show worker pool saturation and 503s: pattern 'worker pool saturated (active=64/64, queue=...)' and 'request rejected: accept queue full, returning 503 (POST /v1/auth/login)', first at 06:54:53Z / 06:55:42Z.
Auth-service autoscaler could not scale: log 'autoscaler: desired replicas 14 exceeds maxReplicas 8; cannot scale further' at 06:57:15Z.
auth-service rate_limited_per_min was ~2/min until 06:44Z, then jumped to ~548-908/min from 06:52Z onward.
auth-service memory_pct stayed flat (~51-53%) throughout the incident window, showing no memory growth.
api-gateway request_rate was ~1250 req/s until 06:30Z, then rose to ~4900 req/s from the 06:45-07:00Z buckets onward.
api-gateway error_rate rose from ~0.2% to ~9% and latency_p99 rose from ~210ms to ~3900ms starting in the 06:45Z bucket.
api-gateway CPU remained flat at ~42% (min 36.9, max 47.2) across the entire window, i.e. the gateway itself was not saturated.
No auth-service deployment or config change exists in the incident window: only one deployment total (portfolio-service v4.4.0 at 05:50Z, 'CSV export endpoint') and zero config changes.
auth-service restarts metric was 0 for the entire window (no crash/restart loop).
user-db CPU stayed flat (~18%, max ~20%) throughout — the database was not under stress.
redis-cache was healthy: CPU ~22%, hit_ratio ~96%, connected_clients ~310, all flat across the window.
api-gateway has no upstream dependencies in the graph (empty edges/nodes), so the traffic surge observed at the gateway originates from outside the mesh (external client traffic) at the edge.

Historical incident HIST-101 (2025-08-14) had the same symptom profile ('login p99 4s','503 on login','high cpu') but root cause 'bcrypt cost factor raised 10->14 in release v6.4.0' (a bad_deployment).
Historical incident HIST-113 (2026-01-28) parallels this event: 'Record market-open volume exceeded provisioned capacity', category capacity_saturation, resolution 'Raised replica count'.
The 4x surge (gateway ~1250->~4900 req/s, auth ~390->~1500 req/s) started in the 06:30-06:52Z window, matching the auth p99/CPU/error onset (06:52Z), i.e. load rose first, saturation followed.

auth-service worker pool is bounded at 64 active workers ('active=64/64'), so at ~1500 req/s the pool and accept queue saturate, producing 503s — a capacity limit, not a per-request slowdown like bcrypt.
